chapter: Leaving the band, Strayhorn and reflections
title: Early tunes as pictures in sound
summary: Greer agrees that in the twenties pieces portrayed scenes, with Bubber Miley.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, I remember reading something where Ellington said and later Rex Stewart himself said that in those days, the twenties, that each -- that the music really had a specific meaning, that a given tune would really be a picture of a given thing.
You know, (it turned----) it got different later. But he said in those years, like Duke said, Ellington said he remembered there was some cleaners you all
passed called Olewando's (PHONETIC) or something like that. And everytime you guys would pass this cleaners they'd go "Olewando," or something.

I don't remember how it went. But he was saying sometimes Miley would come in and he would say, now, this is this guy walking down the street like this, and pick up the horn and he'd play that and then you might say, this is him falling out of bed, or whatever it would be, it would be something where the guys would actually put together a portrait of something in sounds. Is that close to the way it was happening in those years?
The guy said when Strayhorn came in the band he was just welcomed with open arms.
Oh, yeah, Sweetpea, everybody loved that cat, man.
